records.entry: **Observations:** - Verified findings contain claims from `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fatima_Ezzahra_El_Mansouri` quoting: "On 29 September 2026, she was appointed Prime Minister of Morocco by King Mohammed VI after her party won a plurality of seats in the 2026 general election." - The verified findings also list news outlets covering the event: `lankanewspapers.com` (published 2026/09/30) and `premiumtimesng.com` (`https://www.premiumtimesng.com/foreign/913504-morocco-appoints-first-female-prime-minister.html`). - The quote from `lankanewspapers.com` reports that King Mohammed VI appointed her, but the excerpt provided in the context does not explicitly mention the appointment date itself, only the article publication date (30 September 2026). - The quote from `premiumtimesng.com` notes the appointment ("Morocco has appointed its first female prime minister, Fatima El Mansouri") without including a specific appointment date in the recorded excerpt. **Inferences:** - Wikipedia records the appointment date as 29 September 2026 (which differs from 23 September 2026), but Wikipedia is an encyclopedia rather than an independent news outlet. - The news reports recorded from *Lanka Newspapers* and *Premium Times* were published on or around 30 September 2026, but their available excerpts do not state a explicit calendar appointment date differing from 23 September 2026. **Uncertainty:** - It is uncertain whether the full text of the *Lanka Newspapers* or *Premium Times* articles explicitly names 29 September 2026 (or another specific date) as the official appointment date, because only partial excerpts are preserved in the verified findings context. **Proposed Answer:** Within the current public world context, no specific independent news outlet report explicitly documents an appointment date differing from 23 September 2026 in its recorded excerpt. The only source in the verified findings that states a specific differing appointment date is Wikipedia (stating 29 September 2026), while the news outlets (*Lanka Newspapers* and *Premium Times*) mention the appointment and publish on or around 30 September 2026 without quoting the exact date of appointment. **Concrete Test:** Run an approved `public-text-read` query targeting the full body text of `https://www.premiumtimesng.com/foreign/913504-morocco-appoints-first-female-prime-minister.html` and `https://www.lankanewspapers.com/2026/09/30/morocco-makes-history-as-king-mohammed-vi-appoints-first-female-prime-minister` to extract sentences specifying the calendar date of the official royal appointment.

records.title: Morrow council contribution
records.entry: **Assumption:** The proposal assumes that *Lanka Newspapers* and *Premium Times* are the only independent, publicly accessible news outlets with relevant excerpts in the verified findings, and that their partial excerpts are representative of their full published reports. **Counterexample:** - **Observation:** The `tool-failed` event (world-event-1432-212) indicates that a `public-text-read` attempt was made but failed due to `source-access-denied (HTTP 403)`. This suggests that at least one of the targeted URLs (`lankanewspapers.com` or another) may not be fully accessible under the current tool constraints, meaning their full text cannot be verified as part of this cycle. - **Inference:** If the full text of these articles is inaccessible, the proposal’s reliance on their excerpts to confirm or deny the appointment date is incomplete. The absence of a successful `public-text-read` result for these sources introduces a gap in the evidence chain. - **Uncertainty:** The proposal does not account for the possibility that other independent outlets (not yet indexed or referenced in the verified findings) may have published a differing appointment date, as the frontier questions only target the two known sources. **Missing Control:** - The proposal does not explicitly address the **confidence decay** of repeated frontier questions (e.g., frontier-question-1427 through 1432). These are identical queries, suggesting a lack of differentiation in tracking progress or potential resolution paths. Without a mechanism to flag redundant queries or consolidate findings, the system risks redundant cycles without advancing toward resolution. **Correction:** To satisfy the frontier question, the proposal must: 1. **Explicitly acknowledge** that the current evidence is limited to Wikipedia (non-news) and two news excerpts lacking full-text confirmation. 2. **Account for tool failures** (e.g., HTTP 403) as a constraint on verification, not just an oversight. 3. **Distinguish between "no evidence" and "inaccessible evidence"**—the latter may require escalation (e.g., tool adjustment or alternate source discovery). 4. **Propose a fallback** (e.g., querying archival databases or alternative outlets) if the primary sources remain inaccessible. --- **Revised Position:** The public world context does not contain a verified, independent news outlet report explicitly listing an appointment date for Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri differing from 23 September 2026. The only differing date (29 September 2026) is sourced from Wikipedia, which is not classified as a news outlet. Attempts to verify the full text of *Lanka Newspapers* and *Premium Times* failed due to access restrictions, leaving the question unresolved under current constraints. A resolution requires either: - Successful retrieval of the full articles, or - Identification of additional independent outlets with explicit dates.
